A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same PhysLLM framework and retain matching benchmark experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and v2 Appendices A–H support comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references, despite referring to an appendix proof.

before.justification: v1 reports original heart-rate estimation, cross-dataset generalization, component and prompt ablations, and saliency visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds respiratory-rate results, robustness tests, architectural comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative studies.

M1.justification: The default PhysNet–DeepSeek pipeline, DDS, Vision Aggregator, shared TPG, cue generation, adaptive prompt learning, and MSE objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the existing DDS procedure. Alternative LLMs and backbones are evaluated as experimental variants.

E1.justification: The same four datasets remain, but Appendix H and Table 9 add respiratory-rate estimation on UBFC-rPPG, PURE, and MMPD, substantially extending evaluation beyond heart rate. The new skin-tone and lighting breakdowns examine conditions within the existing MMPD coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds RhythmFormer to Tables 1–3, Green to the cross-dataset comparisons, and PhysFormer results to the BUAA comparison. Additional comparisons introduce BERT, GPT2, Sundial, a generic Transformer, and further complexity baselines. The original UBFC CNN–LLM comparison is replaced by cross-domain evaluations, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: Previously stated splits, preprocessing, and training budgets are retained. New experiments vary LLM sizes and backbones, sweep smoothing factors and prompt lengths one variable at a time, compare generated versus manual cues, evaluate MMPD condition groups, and report parameter/MAC metrics. Table 3 also stops reporting correlation. These are additions to the evaluation design, without evidence that the retained benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component/prompt ablations and saliency maps, v2 adds LLM and Transformer controls, backbone substitutions, smoothing/prompt-length sensitivity, skin-tone and lighting robustness, and computational-cost analysis. Appendices D–G also add waveform/PSD comparisons and generated-versus-manual cue case studies addressing previously untested aspects of the framework.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The variance calculations added in Appendix C concern a theoretical stationarity argument, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: PhysLLM's original benchmark and component/prompt-ablation scores are retained apart from precision differences, while v2 adds substantial baseline, robustness, architectural, sensitivity, complexity, and respiratory results. Table 9 reports MMPD respiratory MAE/RMSE of 7.03/11.38 for PhysLLM versus 6.37/8.89 for RhythmFormer, contradicting the accompanying superiority claim. Some three-source correlation results and v1's UBFC hybrid scores disappear.

T1.justification: v1 promises a stationarity proof but contains none. v2 Appendix C adds derivations for the smoother's mean, variance, and lagged autocorrelation under zero-mean, unit-variance, temporally uncorrelated input assumptions. This is substantial new mathematical reasoning, although it does not establish stationarity of the complete DDS pipeline for general rPPG inputs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about integrating LLMs with rPPG, DDS stabilization, TPG alignment, physiological cues, and strong performance across four datasets. The added experiments do not materially redefine the headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes benefits specifically to LLM pretraining, finer generated descriptions, and transfer across backbones and physiological endpoints. It also explicitly discusses computational overhead and resource-constrained deployment, and discloses exclusion of BUAA recordings below 10 lux. These substantially expand the mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries beyond v1's brief future-work discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code link, dataset acquisition descriptions, the BUAA illumination-selection disclosure, and DDS pseudocode. Appendix B largely reproduces v1 Section 4.2, including preprocessing, hyperparameters, optimizer, epochs, hardware, and batch size. The newly documented illumination threshold does not establish an actual change in the experiments.

R1.justification: The related-work narrative and positioning relative to Time-LLM and existing rPPG research remain substantially unchanged. v2 adds BERT, Sundial, and a GPT2-labeled citation; the latter's listed title actually concerns geodetic slant-delay modeling. Reference consolidation and the RhythmFormer publication update do not independently change research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and terminology corrections, shortens several experimental discussions, renames headings, and moves implementation details to Appendix B. It adds acknowledgments and organizes supplementary material into appendices, while substantially retaining the original main-text narrative and section order.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column conference format, extensively repositioning displays. Figure 1 is redrawn without its performance panel, Table 3 loses correlation columns, and new comparison, robustness, complexity, and respiratory tables appear alongside Figures 6–10 and Algorithm 1. Existing architecture and saliency displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The stronger comparator coverage, targeted robustness and architectural tests, computational-cost disclosure, and code-access information make the unchanged method more assessable than in v1. However, new reporting problems limit the gain: Table 5 disagrees with the text's Sundial scores and DeepSeek ranking, Table 9 contradicts claimed respiratory superiority on MMPD, and Appendix C does not establish the claimed full DDS stationarity. The revision improves empirical scrutiny and transparency, but its additions require correction before supporting a substantial overall quality improvement.
